sections.1_problem: CSF shunt distal-catheter obstruction is a dominant shunt-failure mode requiring revision surgery; a standard single-lumen catheter has no intrinsic redundancy — total obstruction means zero drainage. The frozen dossier records the failure-mode family (obstruction, over-drainage, manufacturing) with the clinical benefit magnitude honestly recorded as UNKNOWN until trial.
sections.2_existing_limitation: Existing shunts rely on valve mechanisms proximal to the problem and offer no passive floor: when the distal lumen occludes, drainage stops entirely. The recorded baseline is the standard single-lumen distal catheter (same material/OD/length); no documented multi-lumen floor mechanism was found in the closest prior art (PatentBear specific-mechanism query: 50 hits, none disclosing the full limitation set — see NOVELTY_ASSESSMENT.json).
sections.3_proposed_technology: A passive dual-lumen catheter: primary lumen carries nominal flow; a small eccentric floor lumen in the same extruded body keeps a minimum drainage path alive when the primary lumen obstructs. No valve, no electronics, no moving parts.
sections.4_mechanism: Hydraulic conductance split: G_floor/G_primary = (d_floor/d_primary)^4 (Poiseuille, MODELLED) — the floor lumen is intentionally low-conductance so it is subordinate in normal operation but non-zero when the primary path fails. Boundary regime: laminar, incompressible, steady; the deterministic solver and physical caps are the frozen dossier's governing model (MODELLED class).
